title: Improving Arm Mobility and Use After Stroke
brief_summary: An individual suffering a stroke or other brain injury may lose function on one side of the body (partial paralysis). As the individual shifts activities to favor the unaffected side, the problem worsens. Constraint induced (CI) therapy forces the individual to use the neglected arm by restraining the good arm in a sling. This study examines the effectiveness of CI therapy for improving arm motion after stroke.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* 3 to 9 months post cerebral infarct or 1 year post injury
* 2.5 or lower on the Motor Activity Log scale
* \>= 10 degrees of active wrist extension
* \>= 10 degrees of extension of all joints of thumb and two other digits
* Ability to perform wrist/finger extension movements three times within one minute
